Years ago, walking around Kathmandu surrounded by strange, fascinating and confusing sights, I kept wishing I could just 'tap' one of them and have it explain itself to me. Another time, at a jazz festival in Niš with only ten minutes between sets, I badly wanted to know where the nearest snack stand was so I could eat without missing the next tune. And in Panama, a quiet warning about which streets were best avoided after sunset would have been very welcome.

Every corner, building or landmark carries lots of stories. But each visitor wants a different one. Outside a concert hall, a music fan wants tonight's lineup, an architect wants the history of the facade, and a student only needs next month's practice calendar. Even one person wants different things depending on the moment and the situation.

Those moments pushed me toward the idea of layering digital information on top of the real world, information that changes depending on who is looking, and toward a tool that lets anybody build and browse such layers: no enterprise deals needed, just the freedom to let places speak.

After more than a year of work, Wayfind® (example.com/wayfind) is out on the App Store, with an Android preview available on request, running on Beaconry®, our headless location platform, plus WF Studio, a web console for creating content.
Back to those moments, now with Wayfind in my pocket:
🛕 Kathmandu. The Pointer turns my phone into a remote for the real world: I aim it at the stupa, tap, and its story appears. Tap twice, and every shrine around the square lights up.
🎷 Niš. Ten minutes to the next set. A pin from the organizers: a burek stand 80 meters away, and the sponsor's coupon is collected automatically on the way.
🌙 Panama. The sun sets, and my phone buzzes just before I take the wrong turn: a local left a warning right on that spot.
Now look at it from the other side. If you run a festival, a destination or a town, or simply know your neighborhood better than anyone, this layer is yours to fill:
– your stories, schedules and deals appear where and when they count, in 2D or full 3D, tuned to timing, weather, audience, distance and language;
– your own separate spaces (data, users, settings) with your colors and logo;
– bring in partners and sponsors as guest organizations and manage them yourself;
– coupons and collectibles: another reason to show up;
– no app to build, no beacons to mount;
– you see what got noticed, opened and loved.
You configure everything in WF Studio and publish it in Wayfind.
Wayfind costs nothing during Early Access, so feel free to explore. If something is missing or seems wrong, please tell me. And if you have a place worth exploring, let's chat!
P.S. Later on, the engine underneath, Beaconry, will be opening to partners step by step, for teams building location-aware apps. But that is another story ;)
